project_name: Pleasant Hill Road cryptocurrency mining/data center facility
aliases: Pleasant Hill Road data mining facility
Pleasant Hill Road crypto mining project
status_detail: Local reporting says a proposed 4.9 MW cryptocurrency/data mining facility on about 5 acres near Pleasant Hill Road may test White County's July 20, 2026 data center/data mining ban; county executive said officials were reviewing legal options and were not made aware before public circulation.
notes: Specific developer not found in county materials or local reporting during quick pass; treat as early/rumored but project-specific because location and 4.9 MW figure were reported.

project_name: Flexential Nashville - Cool Springs Data Center
status_detail: Colocation facility at 425 Duke Dr., Suite 400; third-party data center directories list it as operational with 3.15 MW and a 2014 operational date; Peak 10 rebranded to Flexential in 2018.
notes: County site search found planning/community development pages but no project-specific county record in quick pass; capacity/address from commercial trackers.

status_detail: Colocation facility listed at 4600 Carothers Parkway, Franklin, TN; DataCenterMap lists it as a 6 MW facility near the Cool Springs site.
notes: Primary county permit/EDA record not found in quick pass; Lumen location list corroborates Flexential Nashville-Franklin address.

status_detail: Third-party data center directories list a TierPoint Nashville/Franklin facility at 311 Eddy Lane near the Flexential Franklin facilities; no county project record found in quick pass.
notes: Included for completeness because county-level trackers report 3 Williamson data center projects; needs primary operator/county confirmation for capacity.

status_detail: No specific data center proposal found; county materials show zoning/moratorium activity only.
notes: Wilson County Planning & Zoning Committee considered regulating data centers and a moratorium on June 22, 2026; July 2026 commission minutes show a temporary moratorium resolution passed. WSMV reported county leaders said there were no data center proposals at that time.

status_detail: No specific data center development identified; official county resolution asks state officials to pause in-process data center development, while local news says the county judge was not aware of current data center developments in the county.
notes: Separate NextEra/Comstock 5.2 GW gas generation hub in Anderson County is data-center-adjacent and may serve large loads, but local reporting says company representatives stated there were no current data center plans tied to that project.

status_detail: Cipher/Stingray Compute financed an AWS-backed 100 gross MW / 70 IT MW data center in Andrews, TX; SEC materials target rent commencement in April-May 2027 and DCD/tracker sources describe the site as 250 acres west of Andrews.
notes: Capacity recorded as 70 IT MW; gross electrical/site figure often described as 100 MW. Tenant is Amazon Data Services/AWS with Amazon.com guarantee per SEC filing.

project_name: AmpZ Champion Data Center Holdings Lufkin campus
status_detail: Proposed campus on more than 1,000 acres outside Lufkin on State Highway 103 East / former Southland Paper Mill site; Texas Tribune and KLTV report community pushback and county limited authority. DataCenterMap lists planned 2.1 GW total capacity with staged grid/self-generation expansion.
notes: Capacity is from tracker, not county. News identifies Denver-based AmpZ Champion Data Center Holdings and partner EPG Champion Development LLC; KLTV says preliminary tax abatement application was returned for more details and no construction activity was observed at the AmpZ site.

status_detail: Angelina County Judge Keith Wright confirmed HyperDataGrid is developing a data center on Highway 103 West at the old Northern Chip Mill / Ben Dunn Road site, with electrical and water agreements secured and land clearing underway.
notes: 20 MW capacity inferred from HyperDataGrid's stated standard 20 MW facility model in DCD/Baxtel reporting; local news did not provide a site MW figure.

status_detail: No project-specific data center development found in official county records or local/news search during quick pass.
notes: Official records containing 'data center' were county IT/offsite data-center service references or generic state incentive discussion, not a local commercial data center project. Social posts about voter opposition were not enough to identify a project.

status_detail: County-posted Project Raptor public slides describe a proposed Google data center campus of about 2,800 acres and roughly $1 billion capital investment; later local news reported commissioners unanimously denied the requested tax abatement on June 22, 2026.
notes: Tax abatement denial does not necessarily mean the project was withdrawn; county minutes note limited county zoning authority and early-stage negotiations.

status_detail: Armstrong County official tax abatement documents identify Goodnight Data Center Phase 1 and Phase 2 by Crusoe/GN DC1 LLC; Phase 1 states up to 530 MW electrical consumption. Local news says commissioners approved an amendment in October 2025 after the project was scaled back, with site work underway and completion expected late 2028 or early 2029.
notes: Google has been reported as the announced customer/end user; county abatement counterparty is Crusoe/GN DC1 LLC. Capacity recorded from official Phase 1 agreement; total campus may differ after amendment.

aliases: Atascosa County power-linked data center campus
developer: HC Capital Partners; Herrmann Family Companies
status_detail: HC Capital Partners and Herrmann Family Companies announced a large-scale data and energy campus on more than 1,500 acres in Atascosa County, with $2B-$4B initial phase investment and first capacity expected 24-30 months after construction start; county officials later told residents no data center projects had been submitted or approved by the county.
notes: No MW disclosed in public reporting found. County's August 2026 official materials focus on a groundwater information meeting; local news says county reiterated no project had been submitted or approved, so this remains announced/planned outside county approval.
